facts.value: Comparative psychology studies behavior and mental processes across different species. By comparing humans with non-human animals and comparing animal species with one another, researchers seek to identify both shared and unique psychological mechanisms.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Evolutionary psychology approaches thought and behavior from a modern evolutionary perspective, suggesting that psychological adaptations evolved to solve recurrent problems in human ancestral environments.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: The origins of comparative psychology can be traced to the work of Charles Darwin, whose theory of evolution suggested continuity between human and animal minds.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Modern research in comparative psychology encompasses a wide range of topics, including memory, communication, social behavior, decision-making, and consciousness.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Comparative psychology employs both laboratory and field methods. Researchers may examine behavioral differences between species, study animal cognition under controlled conditions, or observe animals in their natural environments.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Findings from comparative psychology contribute to understanding the evolutionary origins of human cognition and behavior and provide insights into the adaptive significance of psychological processes.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick
